title: Decreased GLUT2 and glucose uptake contribute to insulin secretion defects in MODY3/HNF1A hiPSC-derived mutant beta cells.
authors: Low, Blaise Su Jun; Lim, Chang Siang; Ding, Shirley Suet Lee; Tan, Yaw Sing; Ng, Natasha Hui Jin; Krishnan, Vidhya Gomathi; Ang, Su Fen; Neo, Claire Wen Ying; Verma, Chandra S; Hoon, Shawn; Lim, Su Chi; Tai, E Shyong; Teo, Adrian Kee Keong
one_liner_zh: 该文结合MD模拟预测HNF1A突变对DNA结合的影响，并通过ChIP-Seq/RNA-Seq研究其靶基因调控，虽以疾病表型为主，但涉及TF-DNA互作机制且方法可借鉴。
abstract: Heterozygous HNF1A gene mutations can cause maturity onset diabetes of the young 3 (MODY3), characterized by insulin secretion defects. However, specific mechanisms of MODY3 in humans remain unclear due to lack of access to diseased human pancreatic cells. Here, we utilize MODY3 patient-derived human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) to study the effect(s) of a causal HNF1A(+/H126D) mutation on pancreatic function. Molecular dynamics simulations predict that the H126D mutation could compromise DNA binding and gene target transcription. Genome-wide RNA-Seq and ChIP-Seq analyses on MODY3 hiPSC-derived endocrine progenitors reveal numerous HNF1A gene targets affected by the mutation. We find decreased glucose transporter GLUT2 expression, which is associated with reduced glucose uptake and ATP production in the MODY3 hiPSC-derived beta-like cells. Overall, our findings reveal the importance of HNF1A in regulating GLUT2 and several genes involved in insulin secretion that can account for the insulin secretory defect clinically observed in MODY3 patients.
abstract_zh: 杂合性HNF1A基因突变可导致青年发病的成年型糖尿病3型（MODY3），其特征为胰岛素分泌缺陷。然而，由于缺乏获取患病人类胰腺细胞的途径，MODY3在人类中的具体机制仍不清楚。在此，我们利用MODY3患者来源的人类诱导多能干细胞（hiPSCs）来研究致病性HNF1A(+/H126D)突变对胰腺功能的影响。分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟预测H126D突变可能损害DNA结合及基因靶标转录。对MODY3 hiPSC来源的内分泌祖细胞进行的全基因组RNA-Seq和ChIP-Seq分析揭示了受该突变影响的众多HNF1A基因靶标。我们发现葡萄糖转运蛋白GLUT2表达降低，这与MODY3 hiPSC来源的β样细胞中葡萄糖摄取和ATP产生减少相关。总体而言，我们的发现揭示了HNF1A在调控GLUT2及多个参与胰岛素分泌的基因中的重要性，这些可解释MODY3患者临床上观察到的胰岛素分泌缺陷。
